summary: Type-Theoretical Grammar after Ranta 1995: the propositions-as-types kit at Type (every = Pi, some = Sigma, negation into Empty_set, separated subsets); quantifier sentences with the ordering principle and the type-theoretic choice iso (Ranta's 'reference to proofs of Pi propositions'); the donkey sentence as Pi over a Sigma-context with the pronouns he/it literally projT1/projT2 (the pronominalization rule), and the currying theorem that makes the strong reading a theorem rather than a stipulation; text as progressive conjunction with Sigma-associativity as the context workhorse; a deep-embedded fragment with a type-valued denotation and a linearization to word strings, sugaring adequacy proved by reflexivity, and many-to-one sugaring (some/a) proved.

evidence: The pronominalization rule is rendered literally: he/it ARE the projections, and the donkey sentence is Pi over the reified context.
Sugaring adequacy is checkable by reflexivity because both the tree grammar and the word list are concrete Inductives.
All 14 audited theorems closed under the global context.
simplifications: finite toy fragment for sugaring (no schematic syntax, no morphology)
contexts reified as Sigma-types instead of judgmental telescopes
additions: tequiv as the Type-level equivalence vehicle
the fragment tree grammar itself (Ranta describes sugaring informally)

determination_rationale: Ranta's analyses are native to type theory, so the formalization is nearly transcription; the only substantive encodings are the reified contexts and the finite fragment, both documented.

artifact_classes.description: propositions are Types; equivalences are function pairs
judgmental telescopes reified as nested Sigma-types; pronominalization = projection
finite deep fragment makes sugaring adequacy decidable by reflexivity
